subject: Data Engineering
title: At-Least-Once Delivery
description: A quick win: understand At-Least-Once Delivery.

hook.text: The consumer crashed before confirming it processed the event. The broker resends it. Now it's processed twice.

buildup.text: At-least-once ensures no event is lost by retrying until the consumer acknowledges receipt.

discovery.text: The trade-off is duplicates. If the acknowledgment is lost, the broker resends what was already processed.

twist.text: Consumers must be idempotent — processing the same event twice should produce the same result.

climax.text: At-least-once is the most common guarantee because it's reliable and achievable without extreme complexity.

punchline.text: Better twice than never. Just handle the duplicates.

quiz.question: What must consumers handle with at-least-once delivery?
